title: U.S. House · Missouri's 3rd District
area: St. Charles and Lincoln counties and rural mid-Missouri counties along the Missouri River, including St. Peters, O'Fallon and Jefferson City-area communities.

context.text: Incumbent Bob Onder won the August 4, 2026 Republican primary over John Fraser. Bethany Mann won the Democratic primary over Tommy Holstein and Paul Wilson. Jim Higgins advanced unopposed in the Libertarian primary.

candidates.name: Bob Onder

priorities.text: Official House issues page lists Congress, economy/jobs, education, energy, military and veterans, pro-life, agriculture, immigration and the Second Amendment as his stated issue priorities.

positions.summary: Says he will "vigorously fight on behalf of gun owners and the Second Amendment" in Congress, citing his role in passing Missouri's Constitutional Carry law and Second Amendment Preservation Act as a state senator.

As a Missouri House member, sponsored and passed HB1549 (2008) to ban sanctuary cities, penalize employers who hire undocumented workers, and end "catch-and-release"; the Federation for American Immigration Reform called it the strongest state anti-illegal-immigration law in the country.
His official site describes him as a strong supporter of school choice and charter schools, and says he backed legislation expanding virtual and charter school options.
positions.quote: Congressman Onder is a strong supporter of school choice, charter schools, and parents’ choice for their children’s education.

record.text: As a member of the Missouri House, sponsored and passed HB1549 (2008), a state ban on sanctuary cities.
As a Missouri state senator, led passage of the state's Constitutional Carry law (2016) and Second Amendment Preservation Act (2019), and sponsored legislation expanding the Castle Doctrine.
Serves on the House Committee on the Judiciary and the House Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure in the 119th Congress (2025-2026).

candidates.researchNotes: Key floor votes and FEC finance totals are added separately by script.

candidates.name: Bethany Mann

priorities.text: Economic opportunity and infrastructure: investing in union-led jobs in clean energy and agricultural technology, modernizing rural broadband, energy resilience and clean water access.
Accountability: protecting reproductive freedom, safeguarding voting rights and ensuring equitably funded public schools.
Rural healthcare: strengthening rural hospitals and expanding access through mobile clinics, telehealth and incentives to retain rural medical staff.

positions.summary: Lists defending abortion access as essential healthcare among her healthcare priorities.
Supports Medicare/Healthcare for All to eliminate financial barriers to care.
In a 2024 St. Louis Public Radio interview, said tariffs on imports would not hurt China and would be passed on to American consumers.
positions.quote: When we slap a tariff on something that's imported, what the corporation is going to do is turn around and just charge the American consumer enough so that they are making up their profit margins for that particular piece.

positions.summary: In a 2024 interview, said she wants more taxation responsibility placed on corporations in excess of $100 million rather than on small businesses or the middle class.
positions.quote: I'm talking about corporations that are in excess of $100 million, so it's not going to impact small to medium-sized business owners here domestically

positions.summary: Her platform criticizes private schools receiving public money while public school teachers struggle, and calls for full and equal funding of public education.
positions.quote: Our system is overwhelmed by a lack of resources with private schools receiving public money while public school teachers struggle to make ends meet.

candidates.researchNotes: No prior elected office; positions drawn from her 2026 Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey.

candidates.name: Jim Higgins
